plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in East Asian gardens and prized for both its ornamental value and its fruit, which is used in pickles and liqueurs.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Plum blossoms are a symbol of perseverance in East Asian culture because they bloom in the cold, often while snow is still on the ground.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with nodding, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It carpets woodlands, churchyards, and gardens in colonies, often pushing through frost and snow.
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce a compound called galantamine, which is used in medication to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with large, bowl-shaped flower heads surrounded by colorful bracts that resemble petals. It grows in the fynbos vegetation of South Africa and is the national flower of the country.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from midsummer through autumn in some populations
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The Protea genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change his shape, reflecting the great diversity of forms in the family.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad-canopied tropical tree with fern-like leaves that becomes covered in clusters of vivid orange-red flowers. In some regions it blooms in the dry season or summer, and it is a popular shade tree in tropical and subtropical areas.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering in the warm months (December to March) in places like northern Australia and southern Africa
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; cultivated across the tropics and subtropics
plants.funFact: Although it is a showy and common tree worldwide, the royal poinciana is endangered in its native Madagascar.
